header.title: How to Install a Chest Freezer
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to safely install a chest freezer, including electrical work and proper placement.

steps.description: Choose a freezer that fits your space, budget, and energy efficiency requirements.
actions: Select a freezer
Consider space constraints
Consider budget
Consider energy efficiency
Remember 220V freezers may be more economical

steps.description: Determine the appropriate wiring, circuit breaker, and outlet specifications for the freezer based on its voltage requirements.
actions: Determine if the freezer runs on 110V or 220V.
Select 12X2 electrical wiring and a 110V outlet if the freezer is 110V.
Select 12X3 electrical wiring and a 220V outlet if the freezer is 220V.
Determine the required amperage for the freezer.
Select a 30-amp breaker if the freezer is 220V.
Select a 15 or 20 amp breaker if the freezer is 110V.
Consult the freezer manual for amperage information.

steps.description: Measure the freezer and a desired location to ensure a proper fit for installation.
actions: Measure the width of the chest freezer.
Measure the depth of the chest freezer.
Measure the height of the chest freezer with the lid fully open.
Pick a location in your home for the freezer.
Measure the location to ensure a good fit.

steps.description: Cut a hole in the drywall to accommodate the electrical box.
actions: Place the cut-in electrical box against the wall
Trace the inside of the box on the wall
Cut out the traced area using a saw
Check if the box fits snugly
Trim the hole until the box fits

steps.description: The step instructs the user to turn off the main breaker to the house to cut power to the circuit breaker panel.
actions: Turn off the main breaker

steps.description: Route the electrical wire from the circuit panel to the outlet location, potentially drilling a hole in a stud bay.
actions: Run the wire from the circuit panel to the hole
Drill a hole in the stud bay (if necessary)
Leave the wire hanging out of the hole

steps.description: Connect the wires to the circuit breaker and snap it into place.
actions: Connect the copper wire to the ground port
Connect the black wire to the neutral port
Connect the white wire to the hot port
Connect the red wire to the secondary hot port (if installing a 220V outlet)
Snap the circuit breaker into place

steps.description: This step details how to connect wires to an outlet based on whether it's 110V or 220V.
actions: Identify the hot, neutral, and ground wires for a 110V outlet (black, white, and copper respectively).
Connect the hot wire to the hot screw (copper screw).
Connect the neutral wire to the neutral screw (silver screw).
Connect the ground wire to the ground screw (green screw).
Identify the red and white wires for a 220V receptacle.
Connect the red wire to one of the copper screws.
Connect the white wire to the other copper screw.

steps.description: Turn the breaker back on, activate the new breaker, and test the outlet with a voltmeter to verify voltage.
actions: Turn the breaker panel back on
Turn on the new breaker
Test the outlet using a voltmeter

steps.description: Place the freezer in its designated location, plug it in, and test its functionality.
actions: Place the freezer
Plug it in
Test it
